From Wikipedia entry for daughter Ellen: " Her paternal great-grandfather, Arthur Glasgow, had emigrated with his brothers in 1776 from Scotland to the then-large and frontier Augusta County, Virginia. Her father, Francis Thomas Glasgow, was raised in what had become Rockbridge County, Virginia, graduated from Washington College (now Washington and Lee University) in 1847, and would eventually manage the Tredegar Iron Works. Those had been bought in 1848 by Glasgow's maternal uncle, Joseph Reid Anderson, who had graduated fourth in his class of 49 from West Point in 1836 and would introduce the use of enslaved labor at the ironworks to accompany skilled white workers. Anderson was a major business and political figure in Richmond, who supported the Confederate States of America, joined the Army of Northern Virginia, and attained the rank of general. However, because the Tredegar Ironworks produced munitions crucial to the Confederate cause, General Robert E. Lee asked General Anderson to return and manage the Tredegar Ironworks rather than lead armies in the field."

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-902]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Francis's held 1916 Virginia death abstract explicitly names Robert Glasgow and Catherine Anderson. The same couple's 1850 Rockbridge household includes Francis 20, fixing the selected father with both late parent testimony and childhood context.

Selected Glasgow-902 fatherhood of Glasgow-474; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare the original death certificate with the 1850 household.
